statement0:
The word "functionality" is mentioned two or more times in 0.2% of neuroscience papers' Results sections, as of 2020-2024.

Among 2020-2024 papers containing "functionality" , 27.8% of reported significant p-values (p < .05) are fragile (.01 ≤ p < .05) - i.e., barely fall under the standard significance threshold. This is a far lower rate than the median Psychology paper (median shown for reference); relative to other words, papers with "functionality" are in the bottom 14th percentile of fragile p-value percentages (lower = better). Note, strong/weak p-values highly predict replicability.
statement1: As of 2020-2024, papers containing "functionality" tend to be published in higher impact factor journals (55th percentile among all words) and tend to be cited more (56th percentile word). In general, this word is negatively associated with university ranking, such that higher-ranked institutions are less likely to publish papers containing "functionality" (36th percentile).
